name: Concrete Grey
lede: Concrete Grey is a light olive grey matched to the industrial standard RAL 7023, named for the building material rather than any dye or place.

sections.title: A material, not a dye
sections.body:
This grey is filed against RAL 7023 in the German RAL registry, founded in 1927 for coatings, signage and industrial design [1]. The ISCC-NBS system classes the hue as a light olive grey [2]. Unlike most names in our library, which trace to a dye lot, a flower or a place, this one is named directly for poured concrete, so there is no coining story beyond the material itself [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[greenish-grey]], [[cement-grey]], [[moss-grey]] and [[deep-olive-grey]], at 3.4, 3.6, 3.7 and 3.9 ΔE [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: ColorHub's archive finds this grey in 1,634 of 23,781 paintings, about 6.9 percent, as photographed [4]. It peaks in the 1920s, in 26 of 237 paintings, and Meindert Hobbema, Jacob van Ruisdael and Berthe Morisot carry it more than most painters in the set [4]. A grey this common is often weathered stone, shadow or aged varnish rather than any single pigment [4]. The count is a computed color match, not a pigment identification [4].
